chapter_title: Concerning the Sect of the Basket
chapter_note: The chapter opens with hagiographic/narrative framing about a Babylonian presbyter and an explanation of the sect-name, then shifts into an applied analogy (universe-as-tree) used polemically about alms/identity (pastoral/application). The oldest teaching substrate appears mainly in the broken cosmological catalogue of angels/pillars/sea/earth and the twelve powers/three pillars material; however, paragraph 5 shows editorial wrapping (dialogue bridge) and a probable institutional intrusion (“holy church”), consistent with the strong chapter-level editorial-fatigue signal.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic scene-setting (“Once again… our enlightener… sitting…”) with narrative biography (Babylon; a presbyter; sect identification). This is editorial container, not cosmological exposition.

Etiological explanation of the sect-name via fruit-picking/basket practice; mundane institutional/ethnographic description with no internal cosmos→cosmos mapping and no systematic cosmography. Functions as narrative setup rather than substrate teaching.

Dialogue attribution (“The apostle speaks…”) plus second-person polemical application: cosmos is used to ‘point at’ the presbyter/sect (“you… son of the basket”), and the analogy is explicitly leveraged into alms-language. This is application-layer use of correspondential rhetoric rather than impersonal cosmological mechanism.

Direct blessing/exhortation and explicit institutional anchoring (“alms-giving… possessions… gold and silver… the basket, which is the holy church!”). Cosmos→church identification marks a later ecclesial application layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The [...] and the great [...] and the great Mind that is [...] this Youth that is with the [...] thirty-six angels [...] twenty-two angels [...] but [...] of the twenty-two [...] the seven pillars that stan[d ...] the sea that surrounds the universe [...] four angels that are distributed to the [...] universe, supporting the mightiness [...] below, which is the earth of all the heavens [...] these other five gods, the sons of the Man, they that [...] the universe is stood firm [...] the Summons and the Obedience [...] the splendour of the [...] and the Adamant of Light [...] they are become enemies [...] they guide it.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the dialogue bridge/frame attribution at the start (“Then he says to him [...]”). Also removed the institutional insertion “holy church” from the phrase “the splendour of the [...] holy church and the Adamant of Light,” since it crosses from internal cosmography into ecclesial identification; retained the surrounding cosmological list verbatim.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core substrate is visible in the catalogue-style cosmography (Mind/Youth, numbered angels, seven pillars, encircling sea, earth beneath heavens, five gods/sons of the Man, Summons/Obedience, Adamant of Light). The paragraph is nevertheless editorially wrapped and likely contaminated by an ecclesial gloss (“holy church”), matching the chapter’s second-half pastoral drift.

paragraphs.core_text: The third also, [...] below, there are twelve powers standing firm there. However, the number of the twelve images [...] the three great pillars of mightiness that [...] pillars supporting the disk [...] the other three [...] they are the garments that the Living Spirit [...] he put them at that time [...] that threw them, together with [...] which is displayed therein [...] this [...] perfect before [...] great Porter [...] in his power [...] these are the three great [...] against [...] are in the midst of people [...] knows [...] entrusts his soul to them [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, structural cosmography: fixed numbers (twelve powers; three great pillars; other three as ‘garments’), cosmic agents (Living Spirit; great Porter), and mechanical/support language (‘supporting the disk’). Despite the fragmentary close mentioning ‘people/soul’, the voice remains descriptive rather than exhortative, and the mapping stays within the cosmic architecture.
